decisions.name: task_templates table and Task Template CRUD response/API surface
decisions.migrationRequirement: Dropping task_templates would require a data-preserving archival/removal decision; existing rows are present and no canonical replacement reads them.
decisions.externalConsumerProof: Repository-local scans cannot prove the absence of external Worker consumers; zero frontend callers is insufficient for removal.
decisions.serverComputationCost: No change made; existing computation remains part of the compatibility contract.
decisions.reason: 15 persisted local rows remain. The public CRUD surface is also externally reachable, and absence of external consumers cannot be proven. Keeping the table and API preserves future/legacy template data.
decisions.action: Keep task_templates, its repository/service/type, and all five CRUD/list routes. Do not add a DROP TABLE migration.

decisions.name: shopping_templates table and Shopping Template CRUD/add routes
canonicalCallers: src/App.tsx Shopping Add reuse picker → listShoppingTemplates
decisions.migrationRequirement: None; the canonical list and reuse flow require the table. CRUD/add removal would still need an external-consumer proof and retained-row contract.
decisions.externalConsumerProof: Canonical frontend dependency is proven for list. CRUD/add external absence is not proven; therefore those routes remain compatibility surface.
decisions.serverComputationCost: No change made; existing computation remains part of the compatibility contract.
decisions.reason: The canonical Shopping reuse picker reads GET /api/shopping/templates, and 60 persisted rows are present. Removing CRUD/add or the table would break existing-row reuse or an unprovable external contract.
decisions.action: Keep the table and list route as canonical; retain CRUD/detail/add routes as compatibility APIs and cover list + reuse in contract tests.

decisions.name: dashboard legacy response fields
canonicalCallers: src/App.tsx reads homeTasks/completedRecords/passedRecords; todayTasks remains fallback

existingPersistedData.persistedDataRows: N/A; response compatibility derives from tasks/task_records

decisions.migrationRequirement: None for a field-only change, but removal is a public response-shape change requiring complete external-consumer proof and updated contract tests.
decisions.externalConsumerProof: No repository or product contract proves that only this frontend consumes the public Worker response.
decisions.serverComputationCost: todayTasks, weeklyTasks, and summary are computed by existing shared projections; removing one field alone would not establish safe removal of its computation.
decisions.reason: The response is public and legacy fields remain in types, fallback reads, fixtures, and tests. External consumer absence cannot be established, so backend fields and computation stay.
decisions.action: Keep todayTasks, weeklyTasks, and summary in the Worker response and TypeScript contract; no response-field migration.

decisions.name: calendar additive count/status compatibility fields
readers: src/App.tsx calendar marker defaults and Calendar Date Sheet
canonicalCallers: Calendar grid, Date Sheet, Shopping integration, task edit return context

existingPersistedData.persistedDataRows: N/A; counts/status are projections over task_records and planned shopping_items

decisions.migrationRequirement: None for additive response fields; removing them would be a public API change and could require client/version coordination.
decisions.externalConsumerProof: No repository or product contract proves absence of external Calendar clients.
decisions.serverComputationCost: No change made; existing computation remains part of the compatibility contract.
decisions.reason: Calendar response shape is public. Canonical Calendar and Shopping integration remain active, while additive count/status fields can be consumed by older clients; removal proof is incomplete.
decisions.action: Keep fixedCompletedCount, fixedSkippedCount, shoppingCount, purchasedShoppingCount, status, and related Calendar fields; protect with current-response contract tests.

decisions.name: legacy task recurrence columns / enum values
scheduledCallers: notification-scheduler-service.ts legacy path for model_recurrence_type NULL
canonicalCallers: Canonical projections still accept legacy tasks and preserve model-only separation
decisions.migrationRequirement: Any enum/column conversion would require populated legacy fixture migration, scheduler parity, old-row fallback, and rollback/repair evidence. No safe conversion is established.
decisions.externalConsumerProof: Not applicable to persisted compatibility alone; external API clients may also send legacy request fields.
decisions.serverComputationCost: No change made; existing computation remains part of the compatibility contract.
decisions.reason: The local DB contains 17 legacy rows with NULL model_recurrence_type plus legacy columns used by scheduler and compatibility normalization. Converting or dropping them could change occurrence and notification semantics.
decisions.action: Keep legacy recurrence columns, enum values, weekdays, monthly fields, and fallback/normalization paths; do not rewrite existing task rows.

decisions.name: nullable task-record snapshots / calendar_action_date
writers: calendar completion writes calendar_action_date when available
runtimeCallers: Dashboard, Calendar, History, restore, calendar-restore, actor/completer identity fallback
canonicalCallers: Home completed/passed records, Calendar selected-date history and restore
decisions.migrationRequirement: Changing NULL columns to NOT NULL or rewriting history requires a lossless identity backfill for old rows and a proven safe date/completer policy; neither is available.
decisions.externalConsumerProof: Not applicable to historical data safety; old rows are local persisted compatibility data.
decisions.serverComputationCost: No change made; existing computation remains part of the compatibility contract.
decisions.reason: The populated local DB contains 87 NULL task-title snapshots, 94 NULL assignee snapshots, and 116 NULL calendar_action_date values. Current code intentionally falls back to current task/member data and target/action dates so Home, Calendar, actor identity, and restore remain readable.
decisions.action: Keep nullable columns and fallback readers; do not add NOT NULL, rewrite, or historical data migration.
